\chapter{Complexity — Nondeterministic}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Nondeterministic
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Overview}

This module defines nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machines in the sense of
[AB09, \S 2.1.2]: machines with two transition functions $\delta_0$ and $\delta_1$, one
of which is selected by a choice bit at every step, so that a finite run is governed by a
choice word with one bit per step.  It provides the run semantics under a choice word, the
predicate that every branch halts within a given number of steps (monotone in the bound),
the bundled layer of machines with a finite state set, and the view of a deterministic
machine as a nondeterministic one that ignores its choices.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine]
\lean{Turing.NDTM}
\statementsource{Sav70}{pdf-c8033d2fd705-p002-b002}
\statementsource{BGW70}{pdf-b9fb35a232af-p003-b001}
\statementsource{BGS75}{
  pdf-2459e3840724-p002-b001,
  pdf-2459e3840724-p002-b002
}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p002-b002}
\label{Turing.NDTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action}
A nondeterministic Turing machine with a read-only input tape, $k$ work tapes, and a
write-only output tape, over an alphabet of symbols extended by a blank, consists of an
initial state $q_0$ and two transition functions $\delta_0$ and $\delta_1$, one for each
value of a choice bit.  Each $\delta_b$ maps the current state, the (possibly blank) symbol
under the input head, and the $k$ symbols under the work-tape heads to a one-step action:
a movement of the input head, a write-and-move instruction for each work tape, an optional
symbol to append to the output, and a successor state or the decision to halt.  Neither the
alphabet nor the state set is required to be finite.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[One step under a choice bit]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.stepWith}
\statementsource{Sav70}{pdf-c8033d2fd705-p002-b002}
\statementsource{BGW70}{pdf-b9fb35a232af-p003-b003}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p002-b002}
\label{Turing.NDTM.stepWith}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine with transition functions
$\delta_0, \delta_1$, let $b \in \{0,1\}$ be a choice bit, and let $c$ be a configuration
of $M$ on a fixed input.  The step of $M$ from $c$ under $b$ returns $c$ unchanged if $c$
is halted (its state component is empty), whatever the value of $b$; otherwise it applies
to $c$ the action that $\delta_b$ prescribes for the current state, the symbol under the
input head, and the symbols under the $k$ work-tape heads.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Initial configuration of a nondeterministic machine]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.initCfg}
\statementsource{Sav70}{pdf-c8033d2fd705-p002-b002}
\statementsource{BGW70}{
  pdf-b9fb35a232af-p003-b002,
  pdf-b9fb35a232af-p004-b002
}
\label{Turing.NDTM.initCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.init}
The starting configuration of a nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine $M$ on an input
word $x$: the machine is in its initial state $q_0$, the input head scans the first symbol
of $x$, all work tapes are blank with their heads at cell $0$, and the output tape is
empty.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Run under a choice word]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.runWith}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p002-b002}
\label{Turing.NDTM.runWith}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM.stepWith}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine and $c$ a configuration of $M$ on a
fixed input.  For a choice word $w = b_1 b_2 \cdots b_m \in \{0,1\}^*$, the run of $M$ from
$c$ under $w$ is the configuration obtained from $c$ by performing $m$ steps of $M$, the
$i$-th of them under the choice bit $b_i$.  Recursively, the run under the empty word is $c$,
and the run under $b w$ is the run under $w$ from the configuration reached by one step
of $M$ from $c$ under $b$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Run on the empty choice word]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.runWith_nil}
\label{Turing.NDTM.runWith_nil}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith}
\difficulty{1}
For a nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine $M$ and any configuration $c$ on a
fixed input, the run of $M$ from $c$ under the empty choice word is $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Runs under a leading choice bit]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.runWith_cons}
\label{Turing.NDTM.runWith_cons}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.stepWith}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine, let $b$ be a Boolean choice
bit, let $w$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on a fixed
input. Running $M$ from $c$ under the word consisting of $b$ followed by $w$ gives the
same configuration as running it under $w$ from the configuration reached by one step
under $b$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Runs under concatenated choice words]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.runWith_append}
\label{Turing.NDTM.runWith_append}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_cons}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine, let $w,w'$ be finite Boolean
words, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on a fixed input. Running $M$ from $c$
under the concatenation $ww'$ gives the same configuration as first running it under $w$
and then running it under $w'$ from the resulting configuration.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Halted configurations remain fixed]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.stepWith_of_halt}
\label{Turing.NDTM.stepWith_of_halt}
\leanok

Let $M$ be a nondeterministic machine with $k$ work tapes, let $b$ be a choice bit, and
let $c$ be a configuration on a fixed input whose state component is empty. Then one

\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Runs from halted configurations stay fixed]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.runWith_of_halt}
\label{Turing.NDTM.runWith_of_halt}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_cons, Turing.NDTM.stepWith_of_halt}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine and let $c$ be a configuration
on a fixed input whose state is empty. For every choice word $w$, the run of $M$ from
$c$ under $w$ equals $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Halting within $t$ steps on every branch]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p002-b003}
\label{Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine, $x$ an input word, and
$t \in \mathbb{N}$.  The machine $M$ halts on $x$ within $t$ steps along every branch if,
for every choice word $w \in \{0,1\}^t$ of length exactly $t$, the configuration reached by
running $M$ under $w$ from its initial configuration on $x$ is halted, that is, has an
empty state component.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of all-branch halting]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin.mono}
\label{Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append, Turing.NDTM.runWith_of_halt}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine, $x$ an input word, and $t,t'$
natural numbers with $t\le t'$. If every choice word of length exactly $t$ leads from
the initial configuration of $M$ on $x$ to a halted configuration, then every choice
word of length exactly $t'$ does as well.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Bundled finite nondeterministic Turing machine]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM}
\statementsource{Sav70}{pdf-c8033d2fd705-p002-b002}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NDTM}
For an alphabet $\Sigma$, a finite nondeterministic Turing machine consists of a number
$k \in \mathbb{N}$ of work tapes, a finite state set with decidable equality, and a
nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine with $k$ work tapes and those states, whose tape
cells hold either a symbol of $\Sigma$ or a blank.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Deterministic machine as a nondeterministic one]
\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.toNDTM}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p003-b002}
\label{Turing.MultiTapeTM.toNDTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.NDTM}
Let $M$ be a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, initial state
$q_0$, and transition function $\delta$.  The associated nondeterministic machine has the
same tapes, states, and initial state $q_0$, and both of its transition functions
$\delta_0$ and $\delta_1$ are equal to $\delta$, so that its behaviour does not depend on
the choice bit.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Initial configuration is preserved]
\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.toNDTM_initCfg}
\label{Turing.MultiTapeTM.toNDTM_initCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.toNDTM, Turing.NDTM.initCfg}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ be a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine and let $N$ be its associated
nondeterministic machine, with the same initial state and both choice transitions equal
to the transition of $M$. For every input word $x$, the initial configuration of $N$ on
$x$ equals the initial configuration of $M$ on $x$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Choice-independent run length]
\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.toNDTM_runWith}
\label{Turing.MultiTapeTM.toNDTM_runWith}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.toNDTM, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_cons}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine and let $N$ be its associated
nondeterministic machine, whose two choice transitions both equal the transition of $M$.
For every input word, configuration $c$ on that input, and finite choice word $w$,
running $N$ from $c$ under $w$ gives the same configuration as running $M$ from $c$ for
$|w|$ steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Bundled deterministic machine as a nondeterministic one]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.toFinNDTM}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p003-b002}
\label{Turing.FinTM.toFinNDTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.toNDTM}
Let $\Sigma$ be an alphabet and $M$ a finite deterministic Turing machine over $\Sigma$ with
$k$ work tapes, a finite state set, and transition function $\delta$.  The associated finite
nondeterministic Turing machine has the same number $k$ of work tapes and the same state
set, and as underlying machine the nondeterministic machine with the same initial state
whose two transition functions both equal $\delta$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Fixing a nondeterministic choice]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.fixChoice}
\label{Turing.NDTM.fixChoice}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.NDTM}
Given a nondeterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes and a Boolean choice $b$,
fixing the choice to $b$ gives a deterministic machine with the same initial state and
the transition function selected by $b$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[A fixed choice gives a deterministic step]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step}
\label{Turing.NDTM.stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.fixChoice, Turing.NDTM.stepWith}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic machine with $k$ work tapes, let $b$ be a choice bit, and
let $c$ be a configuration on a fixed input. The one-step result from $c$ using choice
$b$ is the same as the one-step result of the deterministic machine obtained by fixing
$M$'s choice to $b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[State renaming preserves a step]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.stepWith_mapState_of_agreeOn}
\label{Turing.NDTM.stepWith_mapState_of_agreeOn}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.mapState, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.Cfg.mapState_apply, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.stepWith, Turing.NDTM.stepWith_of_halt}
\difficulty{4}
Let $S$ and $H$ be state sets, let $\Gamma$ be a symbol alphabet, and let $M_S$ and
$M_H$ be nondeterministic machines with $k$ work tapes and state sets $S$ and $H$,
respectively. Let $e:S\hookrightarrow H$ be an embedding and let $G\subseteq S$. Suppose
that for each choice bit, every state $q\in G$, and every input and work-tape
observation, the transition of $M_H$ at $e(q)$ is the state-renamed transition of $M_S$
at $q$. If $c$ is a configuration of $M_S$ on input $x$ and every state present in $c$
belongs to $G$, then stepping the renamed configuration $e(c)$ in $M_H$ gives the
state-renamed result of stepping $c$ in $M_S$, for every choice bit.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[State renaming preserves guarded runs]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.runWith_mapState_of_agreeOn}
\label{Turing.NDTM.runWith_mapState_of_agreeOn}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.mapState, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_cons, Turing.NDTM.stepWith_mapState_of_agreeOn}
\difficulty{5}
Let $S$ and $H$ be state sets, let $\Gamma$ be an alphabet, and let $k$ be the number of
work tapes. Suppose $M_{\mathrm{src}}$ and $M_{\mathrm{host}}$ are nondeterministic
machines over $\Gamma$, with state sets $S$ and $H$, respectively, and let
$e:S\hookrightarrow H$ be an embedding and $G\subseteq S$. Assume that for every choice
bit, every $q\in G$, and every input and work-tape reading, the host transition at
$e(q)$ is the source transition at $q$ with its successor state renamed by $e$. For a
source configuration $c$ on input $x$ and a choice word $w$, suppose every state reached
from $c$ under each prefix of $w$ of length strictly less than $|w|$ belongs to $G$
whenever the run has a state; then the host run from the state-renamed configuration
$e(c)$ under $w$ equals the source run from $c$ under $w$ with its state renamed by $e$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Deterministic runs under state renaming]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.runWith_mapState_of_agreeOn_det}
\label{Turing.NDTM.runWith_mapState_of_agreeOn_det}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.mapState, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.toNDTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.toNDTM_runWith, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_mapState_of_agreeOn}
\difficulty{3}
Let $S$ and $H$ be state sets, let $\Gamma$ be an alphabet, and let $k$ be the number of
work tapes. Suppose $M_{\mathrm{src}}$ is a deterministic multi-tape machine over
$\Gamma$ with state set $S$, and $M_{\mathrm{host}}$ is a nondeterministic multi-tape
machine over $\Gamma$ with state set $H$. Let $e:S\hookrightarrow H$ be an embedding and
$G\subseteq S$. Assume that for every choice bit, every $q\in G$, and every input and
work-tape reading, the host transition at $e(q)$ equals the deterministic source
transition at $q$ with its successor state renamed by $e$. For a source configuration
$c$ on input $x$ and a choice word $w$, suppose every state reached by the deterministic
source run after $u$ steps belongs to $G$ whenever $u<|w|$ and that run has a state.
Then the host run from $e(c)$ under $w$ equals the deterministic source configuration
after $|w|$ steps, with its state renamed by $e$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Agreement with a fixed-choice run]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.runWith_eq_fixChoice_runFrom}
\label{Turing.NDTM.runWith_eq_fixChoice_runFrom}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.Action.mapState, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.fixChoice, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_mapState_of_agreeOn_det}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine, let $b$ be a Boolean choice
bit, let $w$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $c$ be a configuration on a fixed input.
Suppose that at every time $j<|w|$, if the run of the machine that always uses choice
$b$ from $c$ has state $q$, then the two transitions of $M$ at state $q$ agree for every
input symbol and tuple of work-tape symbols. Then running $M$ from $c$ under $w$ gives
the same configuration as running the machine with choice fixed to $b$ for $|w|$ steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Relabeling machine states]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.relabelState}
\label{Turing.NDTM.relabelState}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.mapState, Turing.NDTM}
Given a nondeterministic Turing machine with state set $S$ and an equivalence $e:S\simeq
S'$, relabel its states using $e$: the new initial state is the image of the old initial
state, and each transition is obtained by translating its input state back along $e$ and
its successor state forward along $e$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[State relabelling commutes with runs]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.relabelState_runWith}
\label{Turing.NDTM.relabelState_runWith}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.relabelState, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_mapState_of_agreeOn}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine over an alphabet $\Gamma$ with
state set $S$, let $e:S\simeq S'$ be a bijection of state sets, and let $c$ be a
configuration of $M$ on an input word $x$. For every finite Boolean choice word $w$,
running the machine obtained by relabelling states by $e$ from the configuration with
its state relabelled by $e$ gives the same configuration as running $M$ from $c$ under
$w$ and then relabelling the resulting state by $e$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{Turing.NDTM.inputSymbol_take_eq}

Let $x$ be a word over an alphabet $\Gamma$, let $m$ be a natural number, and let $c$ be

\begin{lemma}[Value of the Clamped Head Movement]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.moveInputPos_val}
\label{Turing.NDTM.moveInputPos_val}

For every natural number $N$, every head position $q$ among the $N+2$ positions, and
every sign $s\in\{-1,0,1\}$, the position after the clamped movement has value
$\min\bigl(((q+s)\text{ computed in }\mathbb{Z})\text{ and converted to a natural

\begin{lemma}[Agreement of Clamped Head Movements]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.moveInputPos_val_take}
\label{Turing.NDTM.moveInputPos_val_take}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NDTM.moveInputPos_val, Turing.moveInputPos}

Let $n,n'$ be natural numbers, let $p$ be a position among the $n+2$ head positions, and
let $p'$ be a position among the $n'+2$ head positions. Suppose $p'$ and $p$ have the
same value, $n'\le n$, and either $p\le n'$ or $n'=n$. For every sign $s\in\{-1,0,1\}$,

\begin{lemma}[Agreement of one step on a truncated input]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.stepWith_take_agree}
\label{Turing.NDTM.stepWith_take_agree}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.inputSymbol_take_eq, Turing.NDTM.moveInputPos_val_take, Turing.NDTM.stepWith, Turing.NDTM.stepWith_of_halt}

Let $M$ be a nondeterministic machine with $k$ work tapes, symbol alphabet $\Gamma$,
state set $S$, and input word $x$. Let $m$ be a natural number, $b$ a choice bit, and

at most $m$. Suppose that $c$ and $c'$ have equal states, equal input-head positions,
equal work tapes, equal work-tape head positions, and equal outputs, and that the
input-head position of $c$ is at most $m$. Then after one step under choice $b$, these

stepping from $c$ is at most its previous position plus one.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Agreement of runs on truncated inputs]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.runWith_take_agree}
\label{Turing.NDTM.runWith_take_agree}

Let $M$ be a nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine over an alphabet $\Gamma$, let

\begin{theorem}[Runs on a truncated input]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.runWith_initCfg_take}
\label{Turing.NDTM.runWith_initCfg_take}

\uses{Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_take_agree}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine over an alphabet $\Gamma$ with
state set $S$, let $x$ be an input word, and let $m$ be a natural number. For any
Boolean choice word $w$ with $|w|\le m$, the run from the initial configuration on $x$
and the run from the initial configuration on the prefix of $x$ of length $m$ have equal
states, input-head positions, work-tape contents, work-tape head positions, and outputs.
